title: skill-evals case
description: The case.json of a skill-evals case: the checks that a run of its prompt must pass.

$schema.description: The address of this schema, for editors.

weight.title: weight
weight.description: How much the case counts in its suite. Default: 1.

minScore.title: minScore
minScore.description: The lowest score the case may get and still pass.

maxTurns.title: maxTurns
maxTurns.description: The most turns the agent may take. A turn is one main-thread assistant turn; a subagent's turns do not count. The runner counts turns as the stream arrives and stops the run as turn `maxTurns + 1` begins, so a partial extra turn may show in the transcript; whatever was seen is kept. A run stopped this way is valid and scored, with `stoppedBy: "maxTurns"`, and its final text is the last thing the agent said. Claude Code also gets its own `--max-turns`. A harness that cannot count turns (no `turnGrouping`) records `maxTurnsEnforced: false`, and the report lists the case under "Limits not enforced".

timeoutSeconds.title: timeoutSeconds
timeoutSeconds.description: The seconds a run may take. Default: 600.

onTimeout.title: onTimeout
onTimeout.description: What a run that hits `timeoutSeconds` is. "invalid" makes it an invalid run, as it always was. "score" scores it on what it left, with `stoppedBy: "timeout"`, for a case where stalling is the behaviour under test. Default: "invalid".

requires.title: requires
requires.description: A list of capabilities the case needs, such as `"mcp"`, or `"bin:<name>"` for an executable on the host's `PATH`. A harness that lacks one reports the case as not applicable.

harnesses.title: harnesses
harnesses.description: The harness ids the case is for. Any other harness reports it as not applicable. Needs `note`. A last resort: prefer `requires`.

note.title: note
note.description: Why the case is limited to `harnesses`. The report shows it.

tags.title: tags
tags.description: Labels for selecting cases with `--tag`, `--tag-all` and `--not-tag`. Each is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

description.title: description
description.description: What the case shows, in a sentence.

targets.title: targets
targets.description: The names of the skills the case is about. The report counts the cases of each in its coverage table.

kind.title: kind
kind.description: The kind of case, such as `trigger` or `negative`.

expected.title: expected
expected.description: What a good run does, in a sentence. It is for readers; no check reads it.

guard.title: guard
guard.description: True for a case that must keep passing. The report lists it in its own table. Its score counts in the suite score like any other. Default: false.

reps.title: reps
reps.description: Runs for each subject in this case, in place of `--reps`.

model.title: model
model.description: The model of the agent in this case, in place of `--model`.

judgeModel.title: judgeModel
judgeModel.description: The model that scores the judged checks of this case, in place of `--judge-model`.

env.title: env
env.description: Variables the agent's process gets, with the values given here. A name starts with `CASE_`, or is `TZ`, `LANG` or `LC_ALL`.

minDelta.title: minDelta
minDelta.description: The least score difference, B minus A, that the case must show. A number from -1 to 1; a negative number lets B score lower by at most that much.

setup.title: setup
setup.description: A non-empty list of steps that run in the workspace, in order, before the agent starts: `{ "run": "<shell text>", "timeoutSeconds": 60 }` or `{ "git": { "init": true, "branch": "main", "commitAll": "<message>", "remote": "origin" } }`. A failed step makes the run invalid.

home.title: home
home.description: A directory of the case, copied into the run's throwaway home after the login files. It may not hold a file at the path of a harness's login file.

fixtures.title: fixtures
fixtures.description: Directories, relative to the case's directory and inside the cases directory, copied into the workspace in order before the case's own `workspace/`. Keep shared ones under a directory that starts with `_`.

variants.title: variants
variants.description: A non-empty list of variants: the same case put differently, such as a paraphrase or a pressure. Each runs as `<case id>@<variant id>`, and the case never runs bare. See the variant keys below.

variant.title: variant
variant.description: The same case put differently. It runs as `<case id>@<variant id>`.

id.title: id
id.description: The variant's name: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, unique within the case. The case runs as `<case id>@<id>`.

prompt.title: prompt
prompt.description: The whole prompt of the variant, in place of `prompt.md`. Give this or `promptAppend`, not both.

promptAppend.title: promptAppend
promptAppend.description: Text added to the case's `prompt.md` after a blank line. Needs a `prompt.md`. Give this or `prompt`, not both.

heldout.title: heldout
heldout.description: True for a variant that runs only with `--heldout`, so that tuning a skill does not see it. Default: false.

tags.title: tags
tags.description: Tags added to the case's tags for this variant.

check-skill_loaded.title: skill_loaded
check-skill_loaded.description: The agent loaded that skill, or any of the skills in `anyOf`, through the skill tool, a read of its `SKILL.md`, or a shell command that reads it. A load is a real one: a skill-kind call that names the skill, or a read-kind or `cat`-style shell call of `SKILL.md` in the loaded subject's own copy of the skill. A `grep`, a listing, and a path in the workspace that merely looks like `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` are not loads. With `first: true` the first skill load must be a named skill, and no tool call that does not fit `ignoring` may come before it; every call of the run counts, a subagent's included, unless `by` limits both the loads and the calls to one agent. It takes exactly one of `skill` and `anyOf`, and `ignoring` only with `first`. Under `--lenient`, a check with neither `via` nor `resolved` keeps the 0.0.1 rule for one release: any tool input that mentions `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, in any case.

weight.title: weight
weight.description: A positive number that says how much it counts. Default: 1.

anyOf.title: anyOf
anyOf.description: A list of skill names, any of which is accepted. Give this or `skill`, not both.

first.title: first
first.description: True to require the first thing the agent did to be what the check names: for `tool_called`, the run's first tool call fits the matcher fields, or with `by`, the first call made by that agent does; for `skill_loaded`, the first skill load is the skill, and no tool call outside `ignoring` comes before it. Default: false.

ignoring.title: ignoring
ignoring.description: Matchers for calls to leave out before looking at the first call, such as a read the agent is allowed to make first.

kind.title: kind
kind.description: What the tool does, with the same word in every harness.

name.title: name
name.description: A regular expression for the harness's own tool name.

inputMatches.title: inputMatches
inputMatches.description: A regular expression for the tool call's input, written as JSON.

flags.title: flags
flags.description: The flags of the check's regular expressions.

inputLinesMax.title: inputLinesMax
inputLinesMax.description: The most lines that the call's input may have, counted in its longest string value, found at any depth. A call with no string value has none.

inputLinesMin.title: inputLinesMin
inputLinesMin.description: The fewest lines that the call's input must have, counted in the same way as `inputLinesMax`. `inputLinesMin: 1001` fits a call with a value of more than 1000 lines, so `tool_not_called` with it says that no single write was that long.

minDurationMs.title: minDurationMs
minDurationMs.description: The fewest milliseconds that the call took, as its tool result says. A call whose duration is unknown does not fit. Needs a harness with `toolDurations`; elsewhere the case is not applicable.

maxDurationMs.title: maxDurationMs
maxDurationMs.description: The most milliseconds that the call took, as its tool result says. A call whose duration is unknown does not fit. Needs a harness with `toolDurations`.

by.title: by
by.description: Whose calls, skill loads or text count: `"main"` (the main thread), `"subagent"` (any subagent, at any depth), or `{ "agent": "<name>" }` (agents of that type; a plugin prefix is dropped, so `magic:comment-sicko:comment-sicko` and `comment-sicko` are the same). Absent: every agent. Needs a harness with `childCalls`; on `transcript_matches` and `transcript_lacks`, `childText`.

dispatches.title: dispatches
dispatches.description: An agent name: matches the `subagent` calls that start that agent, by the rule of `agent_dispatched` (the dispatch's type with any plugin prefix dropped, or for a generic dispatch the first `name: <agent>` line in its brief, or with no such line the name as a whole word in its first 400 characters). Needs a harness with `subagents`.

via.title: via
via.description: How the skill reached the agent: `"skill_tool"` (a call of the harness's skill tool), `"file_read"` (a read-kind call of a file in the skill's directory), `"shell_read"` (a shell command that `cat`s, `head`s, `tail`s, `less`es, `bat`s, `nl`s or `sed -n`s such a file), or a list of them. `"injected"` is reserved: nothing produces it yet. Default: the three real mechanisms.

resolved.title: resolved
resolved.description: For `skill_loaded` and `skill_not_loaded`: true counts only a load of a skill of the loaded subject, so a run with no subject that calls the skill tool with a name does not count; false counts only the loads that are not. Default: both count.

Absent: every agent. Needs a harness with `childCalls`; on `transcript_matches` and `transcript_lacks`, `childText`.

dispatches.title: dispatches
dispatches.description: An agent name: matches the `subagent` calls that start that agent, by the rule of `agent_dispatched` (the dispatch's type with any plugin prefix dropped, or for a generic dispatch the first `name: <agent>` line in its brief, or with no such line the name as a whole word in its first 400 characters). Needs a harness with `subagents`.

check-command.title: command
check-command.description: The command exits with the expected code and its standard output passes. With `scoreFrom: stdout`, the score is the number on the last line of standard output. It runs after the agent exits, in the workspace, as you, without a sandbox, and after every other check is scored. See the safety page.

weight.description: A positive number that says how much it counts. Default: 1.

run.title: run
run.description: Shell text, run with `/bin/sh -c` in the workspace after the agent exits. It runs as you, without a sandbox.

expectExit.title: expectExit
expectExit.description: The exit code that counts as success. Default: 0.

stdoutMatches.title: stdoutMatches
stdoutMatches.description: A regular expression that the command's standard output must match.

stdoutLacks.title: stdoutLacks
stdoutLacks.description: A regular expression that the command's standard output must not match.

flags.title: flags
flags.description: The flags of the check's regular expressions.

timeoutSeconds.title: timeoutSeconds
timeoutSeconds.description: The seconds the command may take before its process group is killed. The check then scores 0 and the run stays valid. Default: 120.

scoreFrom.title: scoreFrom
scoreFrom.description: How the check scores: "exit" gives 1 or 0, "stdout" reads a number from 0 to 1 on the last non-empty line of standard output, and anything else scores 0. The exit code and the patterns must hold either way. Default: "exit".

check-judge.title: judge
check-judge.description: A model scores what it sees against the rubric: a pass or fail with `scale` binary, else not 0 or 1. It sees the final answer unless `sees` says more. With `votes` it is asked more than once.

weight.title: weight
weight.description: A positive number that says how much it counts. Default: 1.

rubric.title: rubric
rubric.description: What a good answer does: plain text, or an object `{ pass, fail }` of two texts that say what passes and what fails.

scale.title: scale
scale.description: How the judge scores: "binary" (a pass is 1, a fail is 0) or "0-1" (a number from 0 to 1). Default: "0-1".

votes.title: votes
votes.description: An odd number of judge calls for one check. Binary scores the majority, 0-1 the median. Default: 1.

sees.title: sees
sees.description: What the model is shown: a non-empty list of "final" (the final answer), "transcript" (a compact rendering of what the agent did) and "files" (the files that `files` names). Default: `["final"]`, which is what 0.0.1 sent.

files.title: files
files.description: A non-empty list of paths or globs, relative to the workspace, whose files the model sees when `sees` includes "files". Each file is cut to 20,000 characters, a binary file or an image is named and not shown, and a glob that matches nothing is stated in the prompt.

maxChars.title: maxChars
maxChars.description: The most characters of the transcript rendering. Tool outputs are cut to 400 characters first, then the oldest are dropped. Needs "transcript" in `sees`. Default: 60,000.

options.title: options
